name: Supplier qualification and audit
one_line: The two-party approval file: evidence that a named external supplier and a named scope of supply (a part, a process, a commodity) were assessed against the holder's own requirements, were granted a standing approval, and are re-evidenced on a cycle so that the approval can be shown to still hold. Its anchor is neither the supplier's name nor the word audit or certificate: it is the pairing of a counterparty in the supplier role with an approval scope and a standing status carried by an assessment structure. Placeholder template on the fieldless manufacturing schema; fields: [] under PR-6.
design_cite: For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: This row's organising subject is a counterparty held in one specific role, and no canonical key carries it. `client` and `our_firm` are the canonical engagement-role pair but they point the other way: here the holder is the customer and the counterparty is the seller, so reusing `client` would invert the relationship on every file. `institution` is the Finance issuer role, `organization` is only a proposal about record custody, and the manufacturing schema's own `site` proposal names the facility that performs work, which may be the holder's plant or the supplier's plant and therefore cannot stand in for the party. A supplier organisation name is never-alone evidence on its own; this key may only be written when a labelled supplier, vendor or supplier-code slot appears inside an assessment or approval structure.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Proposed TRUE because the supplier is the stable subject above many scopes, many record types and many years, and it is the level a person actually reaches for when asked whether a supplier may still be used. It is a counterparty, not authorship.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Direct only from a labelled Supplier, Vendor, Supplier Code or Manufacturer slot inside an assessment, submission or approval structure. A validated ceiling would require a local supplier-master or approved-list cross-check plus that labelled-role context, because the same organisation name also appears as an invoice issuer, a certificate holder, a shipper and a job applicant's employer. R4/R6 own the rule family; this row supplies no pattern and no threshold.

deterministic: an approval-warrant structure with a labelled supplier or supplier-code slot, a part number and engineering change level, a submission reason and level, a declaration that samples were made from production tooling at production rate, and a customer disposition slot carrying approved, interim or rejected; the disposition box directed at a second party is the signal, not the word approval

an audit structure whose audited party is an external organisation, carrying an audit scope, a clause or checklist reference with scored rows, findings with a severity and an evidence note, an auditor identity, and corrective-action owners with due dates; the same structure with the holder's own site as the audited party is not this row

a first-article or initial-sample report with a part number and revision, a characteristic-accountability list tying each design characteristic to a measured result, a submitting-organisation slot and an accepting-organisation slot, where the two organisations differ

a supplier self-assessment questionnaire with sectioned response rows covering management-system certification, capacity, sub-tier control, and quality performance, returned by a named external respondent against the holder's own question set

an approved-supplier or approved-vendor register with many rows, each pairing a supplier identity with an approved scope of supply, an approval status and a requalification or expiry slot; the multiple rows prove a controlled population rather than one relationship

a supplier-directed corrective-action structure (a request issued outward) joining a problem statement, a containment, a root cause, a supplier response and an effectiveness check to one supplier identity and one received part or lot

template.why: Empty by placeholder contract: the manufacturing schema declares no canonical fields, so no destination-eligible key exists to order. The recommendation held as prose is supplier, then approval scope (the part or the named process), then record type. It is deliberately NOT the schema's default order. The default template's branch shapes are product then batch/lot then record type, or site then asset then record type; this row's files usually have no batch or lot at all, because they exist before and above any particular production run, and a lot-led branch would strand a standing certificate and an approved-supplier register that belong to no lot. The parent dimension is the supplier because "a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child": a warrant, an audit finding and a corrective action are unintelligible without knowing whose approval they concern. Not time-first: "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." Status is deliberately NOT proposed as a dimension even though it is the most salient thing about a qualification file, because status changes and a status-led branch would move a file when nothing about the file changed. The user may reverse, remove or flatten this after facts are validated.

collides_with.signal: The sharpest mutex on the roster, because both rows organise by the same counterparty organisation. Direction one: vendor-management owns the commercial relationship — onboarding admin, banking and tax details, contacts, spend, delivery and price performance, escalation and renewal. Direction two: this row owns the technical permission — whether a named scope of supply may be used, and the assessment evidence that it still may. Same fixture bytes: Vendor-Scorecard_Vertex_2026-Q2.xlsx is vendor-management when its columns are on-time delivery, spend and responsiveness, and is this row when its columns are open audit findings, approval status and requalification due; a scorecard containing both is held on disjoint evidence rather than fought over. Vendor-Onboarding-Pack_Vertex.zip is vendor-management even though it contains a certificate copy.

Reciprocal to the boundary that row already wrote against this one. Direction one: procurement-sourcing owns the competition and the award — requirements, bidders, comparison, recommendation, negotiation. Direction two: this row owns the approval that survives the competition and outlives any single order. Same fixture bytes: RFQ-2026-114_Award-Recommendation.pdf is procurement-sourcing even though it names suppliers and scores them; SAQ_Vertex-Precision_2026.xlsx is this row even when it was collected during the same sourcing exercise, because its question set is the holder's technical requirement set and its output is standing status.

The audit-report structure is identical on both sides and this is the collision most likely to misfire. Direction one: quality-management-system owns the holder's own system — internal audits of the holder's own sites and processes, procedure control, management review. Direction two: this row owns audits whose audited party is an external organisation being granted or retaining an approval. Same fixture bytes: Internal-Audit-Report_Plant-2_QMS_2026-04.pdf and Supplier-Audit-Report_Vertex-Precision_2026-05-14.pdf differ only in which organisation sits in the auditee slot; clause numbers, severities, finding structure and auditor identity are common to both and decide nothing.

Direction one: inspection-record owns measurement of a received or produced quantity — an incoming-inspection result against a delivered lot, with a lot identifier and a disposition of that quantity. Direction two: this row owns measurement submitted to establish or maintain a standing approval, which has no lot of the holder's own making. Same fixture bytes: FAIR_AS9102_Form-3_BPA-210.pdf is this row because its accepting-organisation slot and characteristic accountability make it a submission; Incoming-Inspection_BPA-210_receipt-DN-88214.xlsx is inspection-record because its subject is one received quantity. A run of incoming-inspection results cited as requalification evidence is held by both on disjoint evidence and neither copies the other's anchor.

Direction one: nonconformance-capa owns the holder's own internally raised event and its internal corrective action. Direction two: this row owns the request issued outward to a supplier and the supplier's response, because its purpose is the standing of the relationship. Same fixture bytes: SCAR-2026-018_Vertex_late-plating-adhesion.pdf is this row when its issued-to slot names an external organisation; the internal CAPA it triggers, with the holder as owner, is nonconformance-capa. A single file that carries both an outbound request and an internal action plan is held by both on disjoint sections.

Reciprocal to the boundary that row already wrote. Direction one: product-certification owns evidence that a product meets an external rule, whoever manufactures it. Direction two: this row owns evidence that a named organisation is approved to supply. Same fixture bytes: ISO9001-Certificate_Vertex-Precision_exp-2027-03-31.pdf is this row because its certified object is an organisation and its management system; CE-Declaration-of-Conformity_AX410.pdf is product-certification because its certified object is an article against a named regulation. The word certificate and an expiry date are common to both and decide nothing.

Reciprocal to the boundary that row already wrote against this one, on the same fixture bytes PPAP_BPA-210_Level-3_Submission.zip. Direction one: this row owns the packet, because the packet's purpose is deciding whether a supplier's part may be used and keeping the evidence that it still may. Direction two: automotive-program owns the design records the packet cites, in their own right and in their own files; a container does not transfer its members' facts and members do not transfer the container's purpose.

Reciprocal to the boundary that row already wrote. Direction one: industrial-design holds the document that establishes an appearance standard — the master or limit sample and its acceptance by the design authority. Direction two: this row holds a supplier's submission demonstrating conformance to that standard. Same fixture bytes: PPAP_Appearance-Approval_Supplier-Vertex_PSW-2201.pdf is this row; Appearance-Approval_BPA-210_Graphite_Master-Sample-MS-014.pdf is industrial-design and is the reference the first cites.

Reciprocal to the boundary that row already wrote. Direction one: this row owns an inbound process- or product-change notification issued by the supplier against an approved scope, because it puts the standing approval in question. Direction two: change-order owns the holder's own internal change the notification triggers, which is a separate file. Same fixture bytes: PCN-2026-0331_Supplier-Bushing-EOL.pdf is this row; the internal ECN raised in response is change-order's.

Direction one: public-procurement owns a regulated public competition — tender notices, statutory evaluation records, award publication and challenge procedures, where the anchor is the procedure and its legal frame. Direction two: this row owns a private buyer's technical approval, which is not a procedure of public law and continues between competitions. Same fixture bytes: a supplier pre-qualification questionnaire returned under a public tender is public-procurement's when its questions and retention are set by the tender procedure, and is this row's when the same supplier's answers are filed as the holder's own standing approval evidence.

also_holds_with.signal: A supplier-issued declaration or a submitted study is simultaneously relationship evidence here and a substantive statement about a material or a characteristic there. Shared fixture: RoHS and REACH SVHC Declaration - connector 5747299-1.pdf — supplier-issued and therefore approval evidence on this side, while its substance table is a material-content statement on the engineering side; both hold on disjoint evidence rather than fighting, as engineering.material-specification already stated reciprocally.

Supplier approval is both a quality control and an organisational control. An audit-finding tracker with owners, due dates and management review carries both the assessment structure this row needs and the workflow business_operations owns, when one file genuinely contains both.

A received consignment may carry a certificate of conformance that is both custody evidence for the shipment and standing evidence for the supplier. Each schema activates from its own slots; a supplier-approval fact is never copied onto a sparse packing list because the files arrived together.

falls_through_to.why: A standing certificate, questionnaire, declaration or audit report with durable purpose but no evidence tying it to a supplier relationship the holder actually maintains remains an independent record.
A delivery note, order acknowledgement or shipping confirmation bearing a supplier's name proves a transaction and not an approval, and belongs in the receipt residual.
An audit report or supplier email whose audited party or approval scope cannot be resolved should abstain rather than invent a supplier fact.
A password-protected qualification archive or an unreadable portal export is represented without inferring supplier, scope or status from its filename.
A positively evidenced capture of a supplier-quality portal whose OCR does not establish a supplier and an approval scope stays a screenshot.

sensitivity_why: Audit findings, capability results, capacity and financial-health answers, price-linked qualification terms and disqualification records are commercially damaging to a second party as well as to the holder, and the holder is usually contractually restricted in how it may share them. Social-compliance and site-audit material can name individual workers and describe working conditions. The row assigns no handling class; person names remain search and privacy observations rather than destination dimensions, and privacy policy must run before any model or connector sees an audit body.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH NJ-SQ-1: is `supplier` the right key, or should R1c mint a canonical `counterparty` with a role qualifier so that the seller side of a two-party file reuses one key across supplier qualification, subcontracting and vendor management rather than one key per industry? NJ-SQ-2: approval status is the most useful fact on every file here and the most dangerous dimension, because it changes without the file changing; decide whether a status-like fact may exist as a search-only, non-destination fact or must not be extracted at all. NJ-SQ-3: this row and business_operations.vendor-management organise the same counterparty on the same folder level; decide whether they remain two templates with a mutex, or one template with a function dimension, before either grows fields. Until R1c answers, this placeholder correctly declares fields: [] and dimension_order: [].
